name: Mars Surface / Base Map
description: Global true-color and Viking MDIM 2.1 / MGS MOC wide-angle mosaic displaying Martian albedo provinces (bright iron-oxide dust over Tharsis, Arabia, and Hellas vs. dark wind-swept basaltic plains such as Syrtis Major Planum and Acidalia Planitia).
calculation_method: Direct orthorectified photogrammetric mosaic anchored to the Airy-0 prime meridian control network.
scientific_disclaimer: Color balance approximates human visual perception; high-albedo ochre regions indicate micron-scale ferric dust cover rather than bedrock lithology.

name: Elevation Map
description: Global digital elevation model (DEM) referenced to the Martian areoid (zero-elevation equipotential surface), revealing the Martian Dichotomy between northern lowlands (-4,000 to -5,000 m), Hellas Planitia (-8,200 m), and Tharsis/Olympus Mons (+21,229 m).
data_source: NASA PDS Geosciences Node / Mars Trek
instrument_mission: MOLA (Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter) on Mars Global Surveyor
units: Meters (m) relative to Mars areoid datum
calculation_method: Direct 1064-nm Nd:YAG laser time-of-flight range measurements subtracted from spacecraft radial orbit ephemeris and Mars GMM-3 geoid/areoid model.
scientific_disclaimer: Vertical accuracy is ~1 m radially; horizontal grid spacing is ~463 m at the equator, so meter-scale boulders require HiRISE stereo DTMs.

name: Terrain Slope
description: Regional surface inclination angle derived from MOLA elevation gradients. Highlights ultra-flat plains (Alba Mons flanks ~0.5°, Amazonis Planitia <1°) vs. steep canyon walls (Valles Marineris >18°) and crater rims.
data_source: Derived from NASA MGS MOLA DEM
calculation_method: Derived via central finite-difference gradient on spherical coordinates: slope = arctan(sqrt((dz/dx)^2 + (dz/dy)^2)) * (180/pi), where dx = R*cos(lat)*dLon and dy = R*dLat (R = 3,389.5 km).
scientific_disclaimer: DERIVED LAYER: Reflects regional 463-m baseline slope. Local meter-scale scarps and boulders within a 463-m cell can exceed regional slope values.

name: Terrain Risk
description: 4-tier model-based surface traversal hazard classification (Low, Moderate, High, Very High Risk) combining regional MOLA slope, kilometer-scale roughness, and THEMIS rock abundance proxies.
data_source: Mars Explorer Scientific Engine (MOLA + THEMIS Synthesis)
calculation_method: Weighted hazard function: RiskScore = clamp(0, 100, 3.2 * slope_deg + 42.0 * roughness_index + 8.0 * max(0, (elevation_m - 4000)/5000)). Classified as Low (<25), Moderate (25–49), High (50–74), Very High (>=75).
scientific_disclaimer: DERIVED PLANNING ESTIMATE: This is a model-based mission planning estimate and NOT a certified astronaut or rover engineering safety assessment.

name: Temperature / Thermal Data
description: Daytime and nighttime infrared brightness temperature and derived thermal inertia mapping bedrock exposure, indurated duricrust, and loose insulating dust mantles.
data_source: NASA PDS Geosciences Node / ASU Mars Space Flight Facility
instrument_mission: THEMIS (Thermal Emission Imaging System) on 2001 Mars Odyssey
units: Brightness Temperature (K) & Thermal Inertia (J m⁻² K⁻¹ s⁻¹/²)
calculation_method: Calibrated 6.78–14.88 μm multispectral thermal infrared radiance converted to surface brightness temperature; nighttime IR highlights high-thermal-inertia rocky surfaces that retain heat.
scientific_disclaimer: Represents multi-orbit seasonal mosaics (148 K polar winter CO2 condensation up to ~293 K equatorial midday), not instantaneous real-time weather.

name: Water-Ice Evidence
description: Global Water-Equivalent Hydrogen (WEH wt%) in the upper ~1 m of regolith from Mars Odyssey GRS/Neutron Spectrometer paired with MRO SHARAD subsurface radar ice reflectors in polar caps, Korolev Crater, and mid-latitude glacial aprons.
data_source: NASA PDS Geosciences Node / Orbital Data Explorer (ODE)
instrument_mission: Odyssey GRS (Gamma Ray & Neutron Spectrometer) & MRO SHARAD (Shallow Radar)
units: wt% Water-Equivalent Hydrogen (WEH) & Radar Dielectric Permittivity
calculation_method: Derived from cosmic-ray epithermal and thermal neutron flux suppression (GRS/HEND) converted to stoichiometric H2O mass fraction, cross-referenced with 20-MHz SHARAD subsurface radar delay times.
scientific_disclaimer: CRITICAL SCIENTIFIC NOTICE: Hydrogen evidence from Odyssey GRS represents subsurface water ice or structurally bound H2O/OH in hydrated minerals — NEVER confirmed liquid water on the Martian surface.

name: Mineral Distribution
description: Hyperspectral detections of hydrous clay minerals (Fe/Mg-phyllosilicates in Jezero & Nili Fossae), polyhydrated/monohydrated sulfates (Gale Crater & Valles Marineris), carbonates, and primary mafic silicates (olivine and pyroxene in Syrtis Major).
data_source: NASA PDS Geosciences Node / Mars Trek
instrument_mission: CRISM (Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars) on MRO
units: Spectral Absorption Band Parameter Index (0.36–3.92 μm)
calculation_method: Continuum-removed reflectance band depth ratios at 1.9 μm (H2O), 2.2–2.3 μm (Al/Fe/Mg-OH clays), 2.4 μm (sulfates), and 3.4–3.9 μm (carbonates) from CRISM MRDR products.
scientific_disclaimer: Dust-covered regions obscure underlying bedrock spectral signatures in visible/near-infrared wavelengths.

name: Geological Features
description: Global chronostratigraphic geologic map of Mars delineating Noachian (3.9–3.5 Ga heavily cratered southern highlands), Hesperian (3.5–1.8 Ga volcanic plains & outflow channels), and Amazonian (1.8 Ga–present shield volcanoes & polar units).
data_source: USGS Astrogeology Science Center (SIM 3292, Tanaka et al., 2014)
calculation_method: Stratigraphic superposition mapping combined with Robbins & Hynek crater size-frequency distribution (CSFD) model age dating (Hartmann & Neukum chronology).
scientific_disclaimer: Absolute model ages carry cratering-rate uncertainties (~10–20% in middle epochs).

name: Dust and Atmospheric Observations
description: Calibrated near-surface atmospheric pressure (mbar), air/ground temperature (K), horizontal/vertical wind speed (m/s), relative humidity, and dust optical depth from Perseverance MEDA at Jezero Crater, paired with Mars Climate Database (MCD) zonal baselines.
instrument_mission: MEDA (Mars Environmental Dynamics Analyzer) on Mars 2020 Perseverance
units: Pressure (mbar), Air Temp (K), Wind Speed (m/s), Irradiance (W/m²)
resolution: In-situ time series at Jezero Crater (18.44°N, 77.45°E) + Global Climatology
availability_status: Partial (Archival In-Situ at Jezero + Global Climatology Model)
calculation_method: Direct calibrated MEDA barometric, thermal-anemometry wind boom (WS1/WS2), and Radiation and Dust Sensor (RDS) archival PDS measurements.
scientific_disclaimer: ARCHIVAL OBSERVATIONS ONLY: Shows calibrated PDS releases (Sols 1–1859) and seasonal climatology. Does NOT claim real-time live Mars weather telemetry.

name: Radiation Observations
description: Surface ionizing radiation dose rate from Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCR) and Solar Particle Events (SPE) measured by MSL Curiosity RAD at Gale Crater (0.64 ± 0.12 mSv/day; 0.205 ± 0.04 mGy/day) scaled across global surface elevation atmospheric shielding.
data_source: NASA PDS PPI Node / MSL RAD Science Team (Reitz et al., 2016)
instrument_mission: RAD (Radiation Assessment Detector) on MSL Curiosity
resolution: In-Situ Reference (Gale Crater) + 463 m Elevation Shielding Model
availability_status: Partial (In-Situ at Gale Crater + Derived Altitude Attenuation)
calculation_method: Anchored to MSL RAD surface baseline at Gale Crater (-4,400 m, ~22 g/cm² CO2 column, 0.64 mSv/day) and cruise baseline (1.84 mSv/day), modulated exponentially by atmospheric column mass H = 11.1 km scale height.
scientific_disclaimer: DERIVED GLOBAL SCALING: Only Gale Crater is directly measured in-situ by RAD; other locations are derived from MOLA atmospheric column shielding and exclude unpredictable acute Solar Particle Events (SPEs).

name: Rover Landing Sites
description: High-precision georeferenced touchdown coordinates and traverse zones for all wheeled Mars rovers: Sojourner (1997), Spirit (2004), Opportunity (2004), Curiosity (2012), Perseverance (2021), and Zhurong (2021).
data_source: NASA Mars Exploration Program / MRO HiRISE
calculation_method: Direct radiometric Doppler tracking combined with MRO HiRISE orbital imaging of descent hardware and rover tracks.
scientific_disclaimer: All coordinates use the IAU 2000 planetocentric East-positive coordinate system.

name: Mission Locations
description: Complete surface mission registry including stationary landers (Viking 1, Viking 2, Mars Pathfinder, Phoenix, InSight), wheeled rovers, and the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter airfield.
calculation_method: Official NASA NSSDCA archival landing coordinates.
scientific_disclaimer: Distinguishes currently operational missions (Curiosity, Perseverance) from completed historical missions.

name: Scientific Research Locations
description: Curated catalog of high-priority scientific research locations, HiRISE Digital Terrain Model (DTM) stereo targets, Mars Sample Return depots, and NASA Human Exploration Zones.
data_source: NASA Mars Trek Exploration Zones & UArizona HiRISE DTM Archive
instrument_mission: HiRISE (0.25 m/pixel), CTX (6 m/pixel), CRISM (18 m/pixel)
calculation_method: Photogrammetric stereo pair triangulation (HiRISE DTMs) and NASA Exploration Zone workshop selections.
scientific_disclaimer: High-resolution 1-m HiRISE DTMs cover targeted strips (~6 km wide); outside those strips, elevation falls back to 463-m MOLA.
